extracted.intended_audience: applicants entering the PCT national phase; patent attorneys/agents advising applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the acts, time limits, translations, fees, and procedural requirements applicants must satisfy to enter and proceed in the national phase of the PCT before designated or elected Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of the national phase — applicant responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The national phase starts only if the applicant performs certain acts, either before the expiration of a certain time limit or together with an express request that it starts earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant should not expect any notification inviting him/her to perform those acts; it is the applicant’s own responsibility to perform them in due time. Failure to do so can be fatal to the application in a number of designated States. Acts must be performed even if the ISR, written opinion, or international preliminary report is not yet available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for entering the national phase (designated Offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office may normally process the international application prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date; some Offices apply a 20-month time limit or time limits later than 30 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For regular updates on applicable time limits consult the National Chapters or WIPO website table. ‘Priority date’ defined as earliest claimed filing date (or international filing date if none).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for entering the national phase (elected Offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit is normally 30 months from the priority date; for Offices with a 20‑month rule, filing a demand for international preliminary examination prior to 19 months can affect applicable limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Offices apply different time limits depending whether entry is under Chapter I (Article 22) or Chapter II (Article 39(1)); recommended to enter no later than 30 months to ensure timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reminders from designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Offices usually do not issue reminders that the time limit for entering the national phase is about to expire or has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must monitor applicable time limits to avoid losing effect before designated Offices; responsibility remains even if ISR/Written opinion not established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for earlier start of national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: National processing may start before the normal time limits only if the applicant makes an express request that processing start earlier and has performed the prescribed acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an early-start request is ineffective unless the prescribed acts (fees, translations, copies where needed, etc.) are performed; see paragraph 4.028 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts required to enter the national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The acts that must be performed (if applicable): (i) payment of the national fee; (ii) furnishing of a translation, if prescribed; (iii) furnishing a copy of the international application in exceptional cases; (iv) furnishing name and address of the inventor if previously omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other acts may be required by specific Offices (see National Chapters). These acts are described in paragraph 4.001 and following.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional acts beyond core requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be acts in addition to those described in paragraph 4.001 which must be performed for the international application to proceed in the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: None of those additional acts necessarily has to be performed within the time limit for entering the national phase; details are in the National Chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to perform entry acts
rubrics_metrics.description: If required acts have not (all) been performed by the applicable time limit, the international application loses the effect of a national application before each Office where acts were not performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-performance for one Office does not affect the application before other Offices. Loss of effect is automatic and relieves applicant of withdrawing designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility to request reinstatement / excuse of delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant fails to perform required acts in time, he/she may ask the designated Office to excuse the delay and maintain the effect of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and availability depend on national law; see paragraphs 6.022–6.027 and National Chapters for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: National fees for entry into the national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees to be paid for entry into the national phase are indicated in each National Chapter (Summary and fees annex) and must be paid in the currencies and within the time limits indicated there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If annual/renewal fees have become due, they must be paid before the time limit for national phase entry. Consult the National Chapter (fees annex) for how to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: How payment of national fees may be effected
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on how payment of fees can be effected is provided in the fees annex to each National Chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the National Chapter for acceptable payment methods, required forms, and remittance details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption, reduction or refund of national fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The exemption, reduction or refund of national fees is granted by various designated Offices; availability and conditions are set out in each National Chapter (Summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must consult the National Chapter to determine eligibility and procedures for fee relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a translation of the international application is required
rubrics_metrics.description: A translation must be furnished if the language in which the application was filed or published is not a language accepted by the designated Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a translation is required and into which language(s) is set out in the National Chapter (Summary) for each Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language(s) of translation and choice
rubrics_metrics.description: The language(s) prescribed by the designated Offices are given in the National Chapter (Summary); where several languages are given, the applicant may choose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The language of the translation is usually also the language of the whole procedure before that Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the required translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation must comprise the description (including title), the claims, and any text matter in the drawings, as originally filed and/or as amended; pages incorporated by reference must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Chapters list what must be translated for each Office. See paragraphs 4.010 and following for details on amended material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally the abstract must also be translated, but some Offices do not require translation of the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Chapters indicate if a designated Office requires abstract translation; if abstract was amended by ISA, only the amended abstract is translated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the request
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Offices have the right to require a translation of the request, but most do not require it; National Chapters indicate which Offices do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required, the usual method is to transfer request data to the Office's request form in the translation language; Offices must provide the form free of charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of declarations (Rule 4.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations are part of the request form and therefore translation of declarations must be furnished only when the designated Office requires a translation of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraphs 4.012–4.013A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of claims amended under Article 19
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Offices have the right to require a translation of the claims as originally filed and as amended under Article 19; National Chapters specify applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims as amended are annexed to an IPER (Chapter II), separate rules apply (see paragraphs 4.019–4.020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when required translations of claims are missing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where both translations are required but only one is furnished, the designated Office either disregards the claims without translation or invites the applicant to furnish the missing translation within a reasonable time; failure may lead to disregard or consideration that the application is withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Offices follow different procedures — check the relevant National Chapter (Summary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of explanatory statement for Article 19 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement explaining amendments made to the claims under Article 19 must be translated only where required by the designated Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to furnish such a translation does not affect the international application itself; it may only result in the statement being disregarded by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of references to deposited biological material
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reference to deposited biological material is contained in the description, its translation is part of the translation of the description; if provided on an optional sheet or later, a translation must be furnished together with the translation of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation of the reference is not furnished, the designated Office may invite the applicant to provide it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of declarations/evidence for restoration of priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a receiving Office's decision to restore priority is reviewed by the designated Office under Rule 49ter.1(d), that Office may require translations of declarations or other evidence furnished to the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Office will indicate requirements in the National Chapter where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of amendments annexed to international preliminary report (Chapter II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under Article 34 taken into account in the international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter II) are annexed to that report; a translation of the amendments annexed must be furnished together with the translation of the international application within the applicable time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes Article 19 amendments and replacement sheets insofar as they are annexed to the report (see paragraph 4.019).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of Article 19 amendments not annexed to Chapter II report
rubrics_metrics.description: If Article 19 amendments are not annexed to the IPER (Chapter II), a translation of those amendments need not be furnished to most elected Offices, though some do require translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the National Chapters for Offices that require such translations (paragraph 4.020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — originals/copies and translation of text matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are not required to furnish original drawings with the translation; Offices may require a copy of original drawings; text matter in drawings must be translated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two presentation methods: furnish new sheets with translated text or paste translation over original text and furnish a good-quality copy. ‘Fig.’ need not be translated. If translated text in drawings is not furnished within the time limit, the application may lose national effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements for translations and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation and any copy of drawings must comply with physical requirements prescribed by the designated Office; however, an Office cannot require compliance with requirements different from those for international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If papers comply with physical requirements for international applications, they must be accepted by the designated Office. See International Phase paragraphs for physical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of copies of translation
rubrics_metrics.description: One copy of the translation is in principle sufficient for entering the national phase; some Offices require two or more copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where more copies are required, the National Chapter (Summary) indicates this; missing copies can normally be furnished once national phase has started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of the translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation furnished for national phase entry does not need to be certified by a public authority or sworn translator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if later the designated Office reasonably doubts the accuracy of the translation, it may require the applicant to furnish a certification of the translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of the translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification (a signed statement by the applicant or translator that the translation is complete and faithful) is required by only a few designated Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Chapters indicate Offices that require verification and provide details and forms where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the international application — when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Under normal circumstances, designated Offices do not require a copy of the international application from the applicant; a few require one where the International Bureau has not yet communicated a copy under Article 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicant receives Form PCT/IB/308 (communication notice), he/she does not have to furnish a copy because that notice is accepted as conclusive evidence the communication occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy requirement when requesting early processing
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant requests early processing before communication of the international application has taken place, he/she must either furnish a copy (and Article 19 amendments) at the time of the request or ask the IB to transmit a copy to the designated Office under Article 13(2)(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other prescribed acts for entering the national phase must also be performed when making an early processing request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of kinds of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of the request constitutes an indication that the international application is for the grant of every kind of protection available by way of designation; if the applicant wishes a different kind of protection he/she must indicate that choice when performing acts to enter the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Offices allow furnishing such indications or converting kinds of protection later as permitted by national law; some require it at time of national phase entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming of inventor — when required
rubrics_metrics.description: If the name or address of the inventor(s) was not indicated in the request at the time of filing, that information must be furnished to designated Offices at the time of entry into the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most Offices will invite applicants to furnish the information if omitted, but some will not. Details in National Chapters (Summary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of name and address — formality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The indication of the name and address of the inventor must comply with Rules (e.g., Rule 51bis.1(a)) and national requirements when furnished for entry into the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Chapters provide further detail and required formats (paragraph 4.031 and following).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in the national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may generally amend the application in the national phase; the applicable time limit for amendments may be later in exceptional circumstances, and most Offices permit amendments at any time during national examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Offices where examination must be specifically requested, amendment requests may only be made after the applicant has entered the national phase; National Chapters give additional indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of obvious mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious mistakes in the description, claims and drawings may normally be corrected before the designated Office, presented as an amendment provided scope is not broadened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to Rule 91.3(f); check national practice for allowing such rectification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of authorization of rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated and elected Offices must process the international application in the national phase 'as rectified' unless they already started processing before being notified of the rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Office may disregard a rectification authorized during the international phase if it finds it would not have authorized it itself, but must give applicant opportunity to make observations within a reasonable time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to repeat rectification where authorization refused
rubrics_metrics.description: Where authorization of rectification was refused during the international phase and the applicant requested publication under Rule 91.3(d), the applicant should repeat the rectification request before each designated Office in a language admitted by that Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National practice and law govern whether rectification will be allowed locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: National law governs conditions for rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for allowing rectification of an obvious mistake depend on the national law and practice applied by the designated Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to inquire at the Offices concerned regarding applicable conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review by designated Office of certain international-phase decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated Office may review decisions made during the international phase: (i) refusal to accord an international filing date; (ii) declaration that the application is considered withdrawn due to defects or non-payment; (iii) IB finding that application is considered withdrawn because record copy not received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review consists of examining whether the receiving Office's refusal/declaration or IB finding resulted from an error or omission; procedures in paragraphs 6.018–6.021.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request review and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: To request review the applicant must ask the IB to send copies of relevant documents to designated Offices (in English or French) and must request each Office to review the decision, give facts/evidence of error or omission, and at the same time pay national fee and furnish translations where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both requests and required materials/fees must reach the authority within two months of the notification of the unfavorable decision (Rule 51.1/51.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Result of review by designated Office
rubrics_metrics.description: If the designated Office finds the decision was an error or omission, it must treat the application as if the error had not occurred and maintain effect as a national application as of the international filing date; if not, it may nevertheless maintain effect under Article 24(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If refusal resulted from failure to meet time limits, applicant is advised also to request the Office to excuse the delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excusing delays in meeting time limits — general principle
rubrics_metrics.description: A delay resulting in the application being considered withdrawn may be excused in the national phase under conditions laid down by the national law of each designated Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excusing cannot be requested during the international phase; it may be granted only in the national phase by each designated Office individually. National provisions for reinstatement of rights apply equally to international applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits in respect of which delays may be excused
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits that may be excused include all those fixed in the PCT (Treaty and Regulations), any time limit fixed by a PCT authority, and any time limit fixed by or in the national law applicable by the designated Office for the performance of any act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 82bis.1 defines the scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when applicant exceeded time limit for entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must perform all acts required to enter the national phase and at the same time request the designated Office to excuse the delay and maintain the effect of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure and any time limits for requesting excusing are dependent on national requirements; applicants are usually safe if request and acts are performed within two months from notification or from expiration of the time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of request to excuse delay relative to review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to excuse delay should be made in addition to, and together with, any request for review of a decision declaring the application withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the designated Office confirms the receiving Office decision, it may nonetheless maintain effect under its national law provisions for reinstatement of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late arrival due to mail irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Late arrival of a document caused by delay or interruption of mail service must be excused if sufficient evidence is produced and mailing was by mail registered with postal authorities or notified delivery services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A replacement document lost in the mail may be substituted if proved identical to the lost document (Rule 82).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of errors by receiving Office or International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving Office has made an error in according the international filing date or incorrectly considered a priority claim not made, the designated Office must rectify the error if it would have rectified it under its national law or practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must request rectification when entering the national phase and prove the error to the satisfaction of the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts to be performed during the national phase after entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Once national phase has started, the usual national procedure applies; the Guide outlines only acts for entry and acts that may be performed on entering but can be done after the national phase has started.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants unfamiliar with national procedures should seek professional advice even if not obliged to be represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the application in correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents and fee payments to a designated Office should indicate the national serial number if known; if not, indicate the international application number, international filing date, applicant name and invention title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper identification facilitates processing and payment allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of biological material requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated Offices’ requirements regarding deposits of biological material are set out in Annex L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Annex L for country-specific deposit requirements and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing format requirement (ST.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office may require a nucleotide/amino acid sequence listing in a format other than that complying with WIPO Standard ST.26 (Annex C of the Administrative Instructions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the international application contains a sequence listing not complying with ST.26 and/or language-dependent free text not in an accepted language, Offices may require the applicant to furnish a compliant listing or translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination requests in national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have received a positive international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter I or II) may request fast-track or accelerated examination before certain Offices that participate in PPH or offer accelerated examination based on positive PCT work products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to WIPO PPH information page and National Chapters for participating Offices and procedures.
